principles.name: Intent Before Implementation
principles.statement: A project's intent, risk, and claim strength are classified before any implementation work begins.

principles.name: Research Before Building
principles.statement: Prior art and build/buy/adopt/fork/integrate alternatives are considered before designing a new solution.

principles.name: Research Before Repair
principles.statement: A failure is characterized and researched (prior evidence, prior art) before a repair is attempted.

principles.name: Requirements Before Code
principles.statement: Stable, traceable requirements exist before implementation starts.

principles.name: Tests Before Claims
principles.statement: A test plan and golden gates exist before a claim of correctness can be made.

principles.name: Evidence Before Acceptance
principles.statement: ACCEPT requires admissible, independent, authoritative evidence; it is never issued on confidence alone.

principles.name: Capability != Authority
principles.statement: That an adapter can execute does not mean it is authorized to accept its own work.

principles.name: Execution Authority != Acceptance Authority
principles.statement: The identity that executed a change can never be the identity that accepts it.

principles.name: Project Memory > Agent Memory
principles.statement: Durable project state lives in the event/evidence ledger, not in an agent's own conversational memory.

principles.name: Local PASS != Verified PASS
principles.statement: A process exiting 0, or an agent claiming success, is not proof a task succeeded; only observed, independently checked effect is.

principles.name: Failure Is Evidence
principles.statement: A failure's evidence is preserved, never discarded, before any repair attempt begins.

principles.name: Negative Results Are Valid Results
principles.statement: A refuted hypothesis or a documented non-viable approach is a legitimate, recorded outcome, not a discarded failure.

principles.name: Cost Is Part of Architecture
principles.statement: Money, tokens, compute, time, complexity, maintenance, risk, and vendor lock-in are architectural considerations, not afterthoughts.

principles.name: Risk Determines Process Depth
principles.statement: Higher-risk work requires deeper process (more research, stricter verification), not the same process applied uniformly.

principles.name: Claim Strength Determines Evidence Depth
principles.statement: A stronger claim requires stronger, more independent evidence before it can be trusted.

principles.name: Use Strong Models Where Reasoning Value Justifies Cost
principles.statement: Model/provider selection weighs the reasoning value of the task against its cost, not just price.

principles.name: Never Change the Gate Merely to Make a Result Pass
principles.statement: A frozen gate is immutable for its run; it cannot be edited to convert a failure into a pass.

principles.name: Prefer the Shortest Verified Implementation
principles.statement: Given equally verified results, the simpler implementation is preferred.

principles.name: Newer Technology != Better Technology
principles.statement: A technology choice is justified by evidence of fit, not by recency.

principles.name: Every Important Decision Must Be Traceable
principles.statement: A significant decision records its reason, actor, authority, and evidence references.
